pages.class_justification: No construction: one fixed reduction runs any LWE distinguisher as an oracle on the succinct-LWE challenge, forwarding $(\mathbf{B}, \mathbf{u}_b)$ and discarding $(\mathbf{W}, T)$ — the RTV04 fully-black-box shape, as on the wiki's other assumption-strengthening edges (e.g. ddh-to-cdh).
pages.statement: Hardness of $\ell$-[[learning-with-errors#succinct-lwe|succinct LWE]] implies hardness of [[learning-with-errors|LWE]] for the same $(n, q, \chi, m)$: an LWE distinguisher run on $(\mathbf{B}, \mathbf{u}_b)$, ignoring $(\mathbf{W}, T)$, distinguishes the succinct-LWE game, since the $\mathbf{B}$ output by $\mathrm{TrapGen}$ is statistically close to uniform. For $\ell = 1$ the converse also holds, since $(\mathbf{W}, T)$ can be sampled from a uniform $\mathbf{B}$ using a trapdoor for $\mathbf{W}$ alone; for $\ell > 1$ no reduction from LWE is known — folklore.
pages.sketch: Any LWE distinguisher $\calA$ becomes a succinct-LWE distinguisher that runs $\calA(\mathbf{B}, \mathbf{u}_b)$ and ignores $(\mathbf{W}, T)$; the only loss is the statistical distance between $\mathrm{TrapGen}$'s $\mathbf{B}$ and uniform.
pages.security_loss: advantage-preserving up to the statistical distance between $\mathrm{TrapGen}(1^n,1^m,q)$'s $\mathbf{B}$ and uniform
flags: HIGH PRIORITY: frontmatter `kind: equivalence`, `title` and H1 all assert an unqualified 'Succinct LWE ⇔ LWE'. Only ℓ = 1 is equivalent to LWE; for ℓ > 1 succinct LWE is known only from evasive LWE (Wee24 abstract, via search snippets). The applier sets `kind` from `kind_correct` but never touches title/H1 (EDIT_INSTRUCTIONS § Style contract), so a human must retitle to 'Succinct LWE ⇒ LWE' and re-run generate-relations; the slug still fits, no URL change.

Skeptical-checker lane, parent page: content/Assumptions/learning-with-errors.md § Succinct LWE says that at $\ell = 1$ 'there is no $\mathbf{W}$ block and $T$ reduces to $T_\mathbf{B}$ itself'. By the page's own definition $\mathbf{W} \in \ZZ_q^{n \times m}$ is still present at $\ell = 1$ ($[\mathbf{B} \mid \mathbf{W}] T = \mathbf{G}$, $T \in \ZZ^{2m \times m}$), and handing $\calA$ a gadget trapdoor for $\mathbf{B}$ would make the game trivially losable ($\mathbf{u} T_\mathbf{B} = \mathbf{s}\mathbf{G} + \mathbf{e}T_\mathbf{B}$ recovers $\mathbf{s}$). The $\ell = 1$ equivalence holds because $(\mathbf{W}, T)$ can be sampled from an externally supplied uniform $\mathbf{B}$: generate $\mathbf{W}$ with its own trapdoor, pick the $\mathbf{B}$-block of $T$ Gaussian, and complete the $\mathbf{W}$-block by preimage sampling; for $\ell > 1$ the block $\mathbf{W} \in \ZZ_q^{\ell n \times m}$ is too tall to carry a trapdoor, which is why the trick stops. Re-derived by the verifier; no paper was opened.

sources.ref_file_title: GS08 - Efficient Non-interactive Proof Systems for Bilinear Groups
sources.note: Verified in vendor/cryptobib/crypto.bib as EC:GroSah08 (EUROCRYPT 2008, LNCS 4965, pp. 415-432, doi 10.1007/978-3-540-78967-3_24); eprint version EPRINT:GroSah07, Report 2007/155. Use cryptobib_key: EC:GroSah08. IACR Test-of-Time award 2023 (search snippets).

pages.class_justification: The hypothesis is a hardness assumption over a concrete bilinear group, not a primitive the construction calls as an oracle, and GS08 do not classify the reduction; left unstated, as on the wiki's other assumption-to-primitive edges.
pages.model_justification: Groth–Sahai proofs are in the common reference string model: the CRS is a commitment key, perfectly binding in one mode and perfectly hiding with a simulation trapdoor in the other, and SXDH makes the two modes indistinguishable.
pages.statement: Under [[bilinear-map-assumptions#sxdh-symmetric-external-diffie-hellman|SXDH]] over a Type-3 pairing group, systems of pairing-product, multi-scalar-multiplication and quadratic equations over the group have non-interactive witness-indistinguishable proofs in the common reference string model, and [[non-interactive-zero-knowledge|NIZK]] proofs for multi-scalar-multiplication and quadratic equations and for pairing-product equations whose target is $1$ (or a product of pairings of public elements). Circuit satisfiability is a system of quadratic equations, so every $\classNP$ language has a NIZK proof of size linear in the circuit — [[GS08 - Efficient Non-interactive Proof Systems for Bilinear Groups|GS08]]. SXDH is one of the three instantiations in GS08, with the subgroup decision assumption and DLIN.
pages.sketch: The CRS is a commitment key for group elements and exponents; under SXDH the binding key (extractable, giving soundness) and the hiding key (perfectly hiding, with a simulation trapdoor, giving zero knowledge) are indistinguishable. A proof is commitments to the witness plus group elements that make the equation verify once the commitment randomness cancels; it is sound under the binding key and simulatable under the hiding key.
flags: The sibling edge DLIN ⇒ NIZK (also GS08) has no page; content/Reductions/ has only dlin-to-ippe-ksw08.md. The migration note records the duplicate; a dlin-to-nizk-gs08 page with the same GS08 source would complete the family, and subgroup decision ⇒ NIZK is the third GS08 instantiation.

pages.class_justification: One fixed construction calling $\Gen$ and $\Eval$ as oracles, and one fixed reduction that runs any inverter for $g$ as an oracle and returns its $x$ component — the RTV04 fully-black-box shape.
pages.statement: A [[trapdoor-permutation|trapdoor permutation]] family $(\Gen, \Eval, \Invert)$ yields a [[hash-function|one-way function]]: $g(r, x) := (f, \Eval(f, x))$ where $(f, \td) := \Gen(1^\secpar; r)$. Any preimage of $(f, y)$ under $g$ contains the unique $x$ with $\Eval(f, x) = y$, so an inverter for $g$ inverts the permutation without $\td$ — folklore.
pages.sketch: The construction withholds the trapdoor. The reduction forwards its challenge $(f, y)$ to the $g$-inverter and returns the $x$ component of the answer; since $\Eval(f, \cdot)$ is a bijection, that $x$ is the preimage.
pages.security_loss: none: the reduction preserves the inverter's advantage
flags: The conclusion node `hash-function` stands for OWF, one-way permutation and CRH alike. A modelling defect, not a defect of this claim.

Definitional caveat: $g$ takes $\Gen$'s coins $r$ as input, and the TDP's domain $\calD$ must be samplable from uniform bits for $x$ to be part of a bit-string input; with the wiki's keyed hash syntax use a single fixed key. Standard, so not put in the statement.
